section_summary: This section contains a September 1, 1945 memorandum transmitting a confidential Foreign Economic Administration report on Japanese trade unions and collective bargaining. The attached July 1945 report surveys the prewar labor movement, wartime repression, the state-controlled “Sampo” labor front, strikes, collective bargaining, and dispute-resolution mechanisms. It recommends that the occupation authorities protect democratic union organization, repeal repressive laws, dissolve coercive labor bodies, regulate strikes in essential industries, and establish a Military Government labor section; the section ends partway through an appendix listing principal prewar unions and their officials.

subfiles.title: Trade Unions and Collective Bargaining in Japan
subfiles.doc_type: confidential report and Civil Affairs Guide
subfiles.about: Analyzes Japanese labor organization and industrial relations and recommends an occupation policy toward unions, bargaining, strikes, and dispute settlement.
subfiles.summary: The report traces the growth, political alignments, organization, and suppression of Japanese trade unions, including left-wing, conservative, company, maritime, and fascist unions. It examines paternalism, police repression, wartime labor militarization, the state-controlled Sampo system, strikes, collective bargaining, shop committees, and arbitration institutions. For the occupation, it recommends protecting democratic unions, repealing repressive legislation, releasing labor prisoners, dissolving Sampo and associated bodies, and permitting collective bargaining while controlling stoppages in essential industries. It also proposes dispute-resolution procedures, abolition of repressive agencies, exclusion of compromised personnel, and creation of a Military Government labor section; pages 41-42 begin a roster of major unions and officials.
